destination.name: Croajingolong National Park
destination.tagline: A remote East Gippsland coast of empty beaches, dunes and lighthouses
destination.description: Croajingolong is a linear coastal national park in East Gippsland, about 80 km long and 20 km wide, with the Tasman Sea to the south and Mallacoota at its eastern end. Rocky outcrops, long sandy beaches, coastal dunes and freshwater rivers suit hiking, swimming, snorkelling and sea kayaking. The Wilderness Coast Walk follows the shore, and Point Hicks is believed to be Captain Cook's first Australian landfall. UNESCO nominated the park a World Biosphere Reserve in 1977, and it holds almost 1,000 native plant species.
whyVisit: Walk a wild coast of empty beaches

goodToKnow.title: Bring your own food
goodToKnow.detail: Outside Mallacoota there is nowhere to eat or buy supplies in the park, so stock up in town before heading in.

goodToKnow.title: Unsealed roads need 4WD
goodToKnow.detail: Mallacoota is the only town and the park has no other paved roads. Reaching places like Point Hicks needs a good 4WD.
